title: Server Resume Example, Skills and Duties
desc: See a full server resume example with job duties, skills, summary lines and certifications, plus tips for landing a first restaurant job with no experience.
blocks: A good server resume shows a manager three things in under a minute: you can handle a full section, you know your way around a POS system and you keep guests happy when the kitchen is slammed. Put a clear headline and short summary at the top, then an experience section built on real floor tasks, and keep the whole thing to one page.
Many managers read resumes at the host stand between tables. Do not try to impress with big words. Make the right details easy to spot.
What should a server resume include?
Keep it simple and in this order. A familiar layout is faster to read.
Contact details: name, phone, email, city and state.
Headline: one line that says what you do, for example "Server, Casual and Fine Dining".
Summary: two or three lines about your experience and what you are looking for.
Experience: most recent job first, with 4 to 6 bullet points each.
Skills: a short list of skills and the POS systems you know.
Certifications: food handler card, alcohol server training, if you have them.
Availability: "Available nights, weekends and holidays" is a real selling point.
For the overall layout, our guide to resume format explains why a reverse-chronological resume works best for most hourly jobs.
Here is a complete example you can adapt in the free resume builder. Maria Lopez and the restaurants below are fictional. Keep only the tasks you really did.

Maria Lopez
Denver, CO | (555) 014-2290 | maria.lopez@email.com
Server, Casual and Upscale Dining

Summary: Friendly, organized server with 4 years in busy full-service restaurants, including a 120-seat bistro with a full bar. Comfortable with a 6-table section, wine service and allergy requests. Looking for a full-time server position with evening and weekend shifts.
Server, Juniper Street Bistro, Denver, CO | March 2023 to present
Greet guests, present the menu and daily specials, and take food and drink orders accurately in Toast POS.
Recommend appetizers, wine pairings and desserts without pushing.
Write every allergy or dietary restriction on the ticket, confirm it with the kitchen in person and double-check the plate before it leaves the pass.
Check IDs before serving alcohol and follow the restaurant's responsible service policy.
Split checks, process card and cash payments, and balance my tips and sales report at the end of each shift.
Complete opening and closing side work: setting tables, stocking stations, rolling silverware.
Train new servers on the menu and the POS system.
Server, Blue Mesa Family Grill, Aurora, CO | June 2021 to February 2023
Served a 5-table section during weekend brunch and dinner rushes, coordinating with bussers and food runners.
Handled complaints calmly and involved the manager when needed.
Kept the server station clean and stocked.

Skills: Toast and Square POS, menu and wine knowledge, upselling, allergy communication, cash handling, teamwork, English and Spanish
Certifications: Food handler card, responsible alcohol service training
Notice what is missing: invented percentages and "rockstar" adjectives. Concrete tasks are more believable.
Server job description and duties for your resume

According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, waiters and waitresses greet customers, explain daily specials, take orders, relay them to the kitchen, check on guests during the meal, handle payment and set up and stock their work areas. Where alcohol is served, they also check that customers are of legal drinking age. The table turns each duty into a stronger bullet.
Took food and drink orders in Toast POS for a 6-table section
Explained ingredients, specials and wine pairings to guests
Suggested appetizers, sides and desserts that fit the guest's order
Flagged allergies on every ticket and confirmed them with the kitchen
Completed opening and closing side work: stocking, polishing, resetting
Split checks, processed payments and balanced my end-of-shift report
Best skills for a server resume
The BLS lists communication, customer service, attention to detail and physical stamina among the key qualities for the job. Mix those with practical skills.
POS systems (name them: Toast, Square, Aloha, Clover...)
Menu, wine, beer and cocktail knowledge
Clear communication with guests and the kitchen
Teamwork with bussers, hosts and cooks
My advice: pick the 8 to 10 that appear in the job posting and that you can prove with an example. A list of 25 skills looks padded.
Server resume summary and headline examples
Your headline is a single line under your name. Your summary is two or three sentences. For more ideas, see our resume summary examples.

Headline: Entry-Level Server | Customer Service and Teamwork
Summary: Dependable cashier with 1 year at a busy coffee shop, strong cash handling skills and a food handler card. Available nights and weekends to start as a server or server assistant.

Headline: Experienced Server | Fine Dining and Full Bar
Summary: Server with 6 years in upscale restaurants, confident with wine service, multi-course menus and large parties. Known for careful allergy handling and for training new staff. Seeking a lead server role in a chef-driven restaurant.
Certifications that help a server resume
Rules depend on your state, county and sometimes city, so check locally. Even when optional, these show you are ready on day one.

Food handler card: the BLS notes that some states require servers to take food safety training. California, for example, requires most food handlers to get a card within 30 days of hire, according to the Orange County Health Care Agency.

Responsible alcohol service training: some states, counties and cities require it for anyone who serves alcohol, and many employers ask for it anyway. The BLS also notes that most states require alcohol servers to be at least 18.
How to write a server resume with no experience

Plenty of servers start with no restaurant job at all. The BLS says no formal education is typically required and that training usually happens on the job. So prove you learn fast and treat people well.
Use any customer-facing job: retail, fast food, cashier, front desk, babysitting.
Add volunteering or events where you served food, like a church dinner or a school fundraiser.
Get a food handler card before you apply if your state requires one. It shows initiative.
Apply for host, busser or food runner roles too. They are a common way into serving.
Changing careers? Lead with what transfers. A retail associate already knows how to suggest add-ons without being pushy. Say that in your summary.
Listing duties with no detail, like "served customers". Every server did that.
Inventing numbers such as tip averages or sales increases you cannot back up.
Forgetting the POS systems you know. Managers look for them first.
Sending a two-page resume. One page is enough for almost every server.

What is the best objective for a server resume?
Most managers prefer a short summary. Say how long you have served, what kind of restaurant you know and what shifts you can work.
Should I put my tips on my server resume?
Usually not. Describe your section size and the pace of the restaurant instead.
Do I need a cover letter to apply as a server?
Not always. If the posting asks for one, keep it short and mention the restaurant by name.
